name: Terminal
description: Drive terminals the user watches: open Claude Code (or Codex/opencode) and give it tasks, or run shell commands. terminal-create agent="claude" starts Claude Code on the workspace owner's Anthropic API key; terminal-prompt sends a task and waits for its turn to end; terminal-run runs a command and returns its output; terminal-wait waits for a state; terminal-screen shows the screen. Each session has its own window with an "Agent" / "Agent off" switch. Requires the Bash app (mca.teros.bash).

changelog.notes: Two spaces: a terminal is either a person's personal terminal (their own machine, home and logins) or a shared terminal in the workspace's machine, which every member with write access sees and types in. A person can open a shared terminal only where the workspace's Bash app is shared; the sessions an agent opens are always shared and do not depend on that. terminal-list says which space each session is in. Both kinds stay closed to agents while they read "Agent off". A person can let the workspace watch their personal terminal; that is view only for the others and does not open it to agents.

Terminal windows: each session has its own Terminal window and one "Agent" / "Agent off" switch, on in the sessions an agent opens and off in the sessions a person opens. The two tools for asking for a session and letting go of it are now terminal-request-control and terminal-release-control; the person answers a request with "Allow" / "Keep off". A session a person opens is private to them and closed to agents until they switch it to "Agent"; the sessions agents open are visible to the workspace's members. Teros no longer handles any Claude sign-in and the tool that asked for one is gone: the Claude Code sessions an agent opens run on the API key of the workspace owner's Anthropic provider, and on a login screen the agent stops and tells the user.

A woken session's note says 'same directory' only when its old directory came back (otherwise: back in /workspace). A request for a session is answered only by the person typing in it, or else by whoever opened it; the chat card keeps how the request ended, also after a reload. Tool descriptions say sessions wake in the same directory while it still exists. The tools that ask for a session and let go of it are marked safe writes, not read-only: they still run without an approval.

The agent can let go of a session when asked and is told what the person clicks. A note the person leaves now reaches the agent on any tool (run, write…). A second agent asking while a request is pending hears 'busy'. A refused write ends with one next step; closing an unknown id is an error.

In a session a person is using, the agent asks before typing and the person answers in the chat and the Terminal window. Refused writes and a wait ended by a person typing name the asking tool as the next step.
The bridge only reaches this workspace's sessions.

Sessions never expire any more, and pin is gone: idle sessions sleep instead. After 15 min with no input, output or viewer the workspace's terminal machine is frozen (no CPU, nothing lost); after 2 h frozen each session is saved and the machine stops. Every tool that uses a session (terminal-prompt, -run, -write, -send-key, -screen, -read, -wait, -wait-for) wakes it first and says so: a sleeping session comes back in the same directory with its old output shown dimmed, Claude Code resumes its conversation, and a program that was running (e.g. a dev server) is reported as not restarted. terminal-list shows frozen and sleeping sessions. terminal-create no longer takes pinned (still accepted, ignored).

Agent-first tools. New terminal-prompt (send a task to Claude Code/Codex/opencode and wait for its turn to end), terminal-wait (wait for a coding agent's turn, a ready agent, a finished command, quiet output or screen text — no sleeping or polling), terminal-run (run a shell command, get its output) and terminal-show (bring a session up in the user's Terminal window). terminal-create takes agent=claude|codex|opencode and returns once the agent is ready, shows the session in the user's window by default and gives every session a real title. Answers are plain text for the model (what happened, the screen, the next step) with the same data as structuredContent. terminal-send-key knows shift-tab, backspace, delete, home/end, page keys, F-keys, ctrl-<letter>, alt-<key> and key sequences. Multi-line text is pasted as one block into programs that support it.

Sessions live in the workspace's terminal host (tmux): they survive backend restarts and the user watches/types in the same session from the Terminal window. New terminal-screen tool (rendered screen: rows, cursor, title, foreground command). terminal-create takes title and pinned; terminal-list reports title, command, agent state, pinned and watchers.

The bridge only allows terminal.* backend actions (admin-api.* was declared but never used). Host shells were removed with mca.teros.admin.bash (2026-10-19): terminal sessions run in the workspace bash container.

terminal-wait-for now matches interactive prompts ("››› ", "$ ") that never end in newline: PtyManager evaluates the pending partial line as a virtual buffer line. E2E validated: integration suite (6 tests, scripted PTYs) + real-PTY smoke (scripts/smoke-terminal-mca.mts under node/tsx — bun+node-pty is unstable).
Initial release — create, write, read, wait-for, list and destroy interactive PTY sessions hosted in the workspace bash container
